content:
A voice resembling that of Phra Dhammachayo, the former abbot of Wat Phra Dhammakaya who has not appeared publicly for nearly a decade, was heard during a religious ceremony broadcast by the temple on November 5, 2026, renewing public interest in his whereabouts.
The development comes months after prosecutors discontinued criminal proceedings against the former abbot over alleged money laundering and receiving stolen property linked to the Klongchan Credit Union Cooperative scandal. The case was terminated in March after its 15-year limitation period expired.
Wat Phra Dhammakaya’s Corporate Communications Office livestreamed a ceremony on Facebook featuring clockwise circumambulation, chanting of the Dhammachakka, meditation, prayers and the spreading of loving-kindness.
During part of the broadcast, viewers heard a voice that closely resembled Phra Dhammachayo delivering a Buddhist sermon.
The speaker's tone and use of the expression “na ja”, a phrase closely associated with the former abbot, drew particular attention among his followers.
However, Phra Dhammachayo did not appear on screen at any point during the sermon.
It remains unclear whether the temple played an earlier recording of his teachings or whether the audio was recorded recently. No information has been provided to establish when the sermon was delivered.
The YouTube channel GBNUS LIVE also published a video combining still images with audio of a sermon attributed to Phra Dhammachayo. The recording dates of the images and audio have not been independently established.
The broadcast has revived questions about the former abbot, whose whereabouts have remained unconfirmed since authorities attempted to arrest him almost 10 years ago.
Phra Dhammachayo became the subject of a major criminal investigation following allegations of financial irregularities involving the Klongchan Credit Union Cooperative.
Investigators examining the cooperative's financial transactions identified cheques issued by Supachai Srisupa-aksorn, its former chairman, to various individuals and organisations.
The financial trail included donations associated with Phra Dhammachayo and Wat Phra Dhammakaya, prompting the Department of Special Investigation (DSI) to examine the former abbot's involvement.
The DSI investigated allegations of conspiracy to launder money, joint money laundering and receiving stolen property.
As part of its investigation, the department summoned Phra Dhammachayo for questioning on three occasions: April 8, April 25 and May 16, 2016.
He failed to appear before investigators on each occasion.
His legal representatives and Wat Phra Dhammakaya maintained that he was suffering from health problems and was unable to travel to acknowledge the allegations.
The DSI, however, insisted that the former abbot was required to enter the criminal justice process.
Following his failure to respond to the summonses, the Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant on May 17, 2016, at the DSI's request.
Authorities subsequently made several attempts to locate and apprehend him, including operations at Wat Phra Dhammakaya.
Their efforts encountered resistance from large numbers of temple followers who gathered to oppose the authorities' entry into the compound.
The confrontation escalated in February 2017 when the government of then-prime minister General Prayut Chan-o-cha invoked Article 44 of the interim constitution to designate Wat Phra Dhammakaya and surrounding areas as a controlled zone.
The measure allowed security personnel and investigators to carry out an extensive operation to search for Phra Dhammachayo.
Large numbers of officers were deployed around the temple, where they encountered resistance from followers gathered inside and outside the compound.
The operation attracted considerable public attention as authorities searched multiple locations within the temple grounds.
Despite the extensive searches, officers failed to locate or arrest the former abbot.
His whereabouts remained unknown after the operation was brought to an end.
Phra Dhammachayo also lost his senior ecclesiastical rank in March 2017. The royal order removing his rank took effect on March 4, following his failure to surrender under the arrest warrant.
The removal concerned his ecclesiastical title and did not constitute an order requiring him to leave the monkhood.
Since then, reports concerning the former abbot have surfaced periodically, but there has been no confirmed public appearance or reliable information establishing his location.
A significant development emerged on March 26, 2026, when the DSI disclosed that it had received notification of a decision by prosecutors to discontinue proceedings against Phra Dhammachayo and another suspect.
The notification, dated March 20, came from the Office of the Special Prosecutor for Special Cases 4.
It confirmed that proceedings involving allegations of conspiracy to launder money, joint money laundering and receiving stolen property had been terminated because the statutory limitation period had expired.
Although the Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant in 2016, the 15-year limitation period was not calculated from that date.
Instead, the period began when the alleged offences occurred.
According to the DSI, the relevant period was calculated from the final cheque transaction in 2011, meaning the 15-year deadline expired in 2026.
Despite efforts to locate Phra Dhammachayo following the issuance of the arrest warrant, investigators were unable to bring him before the court for prosecution within the legally prescribed period.
The expiry of the limitation period consequently ended the authorities' ability to pursue the specified criminal charges.
The prosecutors' decision was not an acquittal or a court ruling that Phra Dhammachayo had committed no offence. It meant that criminal proceedings on those charges could no longer continue because the statutory deadline had passed.
The termination of the criminal case also did not automatically bring all related legal proceedings to an end.
The Anti-Money Laundering Office (AMLO) has continued separate civil proceedings concerning assets linked to the wider investigation.
Phra Dhammachayo, now 82, has not made a confirmed public appearance since the authorities' unsuccessful attempts to apprehend him.
The November 5 broadcast has therefore attracted renewed attention, particularly because it featured a voice resembling his without showing him participating in the ceremony.
Questions remain over whether the sermon was recorded recently or was an earlier recording played during the religious proceedings.
Nearly a decade after the 2016 arrest warrant and the extensive temple searches in 2017, the former abbot's location remains unconfirmed.
Although the money-laundering and receiving-stolen-property case was terminated in March 2026, the latest audio has provided no conclusive evidence that Phra Dhammachayo has returned to public life.
summary: A voice resembling that of Phra Dhammachayo, the former abbot of Wat Phra Dhammakaya who has not appeared publicly for nearly a decade, was heard during a religious ceremony broadcast by the temple on November 5, 2026, renewing public interest in his whereabouts.

content:
Paraguay’s rightwing president, Santiago Peña, resigned on Thursday after a political and financial crisis collapsed the South American country’s banking system in recent days.
At the centre of the crisis is Ueno Bank, which in just a few years under Peña went from an obscure digital bank to one of the country’s largest lenders, claiming to have about 60% of Paraguay’s adult population as customers.
Last Monday, the central bank ordered Ueno into resolution over insolvency, freezing the deposits of 3 million customers, leaving hundreds of thousands of families without access to money for food and basic daily expenses. Bank executives were arrested, and people took to the streets in massive protests.
In power since August 2023 and with a term running until 2028, the 47-year-old economist was already facing impeachment proceedings that had broad support.
“Dear compatriots, today I address you at one of the most difficult moments of my life. With my heart set on Paraguay and with the conviction that our republic must always come before any person or circumstance, I have decided to submit my resignation as president of the republic,” said Peña in a video.
Thousands of Paraguayans gathered outside Congress on Thursday to protest against Peña. Lawmakers voted unanimously on Thursday to launch impeachment proceedings against Peña over the crisis, alleging misconduct and a conflict of interest in dealings with the bank to which he is tied.
Ueno Bank began as a finance company in the 1970s and, in 2021, was bought by Grupo Vázquez, one of Paraguay’s largest business and industrial conglomerates. At the end of 2023, it received authorisation from the central bank, already under Peña’s administration, to operate as a digital bank.
The bank rapidly expanded its operations, attracting customers with generous cash-back offers on groceries and sponsoring Paraguay’s national football team. On Wednesday, the players released a letter “demanding” a “forceful response” from the government and the justice system.
The bank came to manage between $800m and $850m in deposits from state and pension entities, including retirement funds, prompting criticism over conflicts of interest because of Peña’s previous shareholding ties to Ueno Holding.
Peña said that, as an economist, he had merely made an “investment”, but that he had already disposed of all his shares. When the local press pointed to possible improper favouritism in directing state and pension funds to the bank, he called it a “false media campaign” aimed at weakening his government.
On Wednesday, opposition lawmakers and even members of Peña’s Colorado party filed an impeachment motion holding the president responsible for the collapse. He had been a shareholder in the group that ran the bank until early last year and, in recent months, had reportedly been ignoring warnings from the central bank and the media about its operations.
Political pressure intensified on Thursday morning when the ex-president Horacio Cartes, his former ally, posted a message endorsing the impeachment.
“We will not stand on the side of the theft of public, private and pensioners’ funds. We must think of the people and of the values we uphold in the Colorado party. We support the impeachment of the president of the republic, Santiago Peña, in order to restore the institutional order of the republic,” he wrote.
Other lawmakers followed suit and began debating impeachment when Peña released a video announcing his resignation.
“I do so thinking of the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions,” said the now former president.
“I also want to apologise to the people if at any point I failed them … But today my priority is only one thing: the peace of mind of Paraguayans who trusted their savings to our financial system … My greatest wish is that the return of those funds is guaranteed,” he added.
Since the scandal broke, Peña has insisted in interviews and statements that he committed no wrongdoing.
Opposition senator Rafael Filizzola called the case “the biggest fraud carried out from political power in the democratic era … This is a bank created from political power, to use public money for private businesses linked to political power, with the president of the republic at the head of it,” he told 1020 AM radio.
Peña, a former finance minister who promised to rebuild a “great Paraguay”, was a key ally of the US president, Donald Trump, in the region – one of the few Latin American presidents to attend Trump’s second inauguration. US officials, including the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, repeatedly praised him as a “strategic partner”, and Peña recently flew to Washington to discuss critical minerals and economic cooperation. Neither Rubio nor Trump has yet commented on Peña’s resignation.
It is still unclear who will replace him or when, because his resignation must, in theory, be accepted by Congress – in which case the vice-president, Pedro Alliana, would take over. Alliana is also suspected of involvement in the Ueno Bank scandal, which he has denied.
About an hour after Peña’s announcement, the lower house unanimously approved the impeachment motion, which now goes to the senate. If approved, even after his resignation, he would lose his senate seat and, with it, parliamentary immunity, leaving him to face any criminal proceedings in the ordinary courts.
summary: Santiago Peña’s rightwing administration had authorised Ueno Bank to drastically expand operations before collapse Paraguay’s rightwing president, Santiago Peña, resigned on Thursday after a political and financial crisis collapsed the South American country’s banking system in recent days. At the centre of the crisis is Ueno Bank, which in just a few years under Peña went from an obscure digital bank to one of the country’s largest lenders, claiming to have about 60% of Paraguay’s adult population as customers. content:
One of the UK's smallest accredited zoos is celebrating after "extra special" pied tamarin twins were born at the site.
Shaldon Wildlife Trust, in Devon, said the critically endangered twins were born on 29 September to mum Bobby and dad Pedra. Its director, Zak Showell, said it was a "challenge" to breed the species.
The trust said the animals were among the most endangered primates in South America. Bosses said the infants were "thriving" and had started to hitch rides on their parents' backs as they explored their habitat.
Showell said: "For a zoo of our size to achieve this and to be one of just two European zoos to manage it this year is an unbelievable proud moment for our small team."
The trust said pied tamarins required "stress-free environments and specialist care"
"It has been an incredible year for births here at Shaldon, but these twins are extra special," he said.
"Pied tamarins are exceptionally delicate animals, and breeding them successfully is a challenge."
The trust said the primates required "stress-free environments and specialist care".
It said zoo keepers intentionally kept the news of the arrivals under wraps for a few weeks to give the "delicate family complete peace and quiet".
The species is listed as critically endangered on the International Union of Conservation and Nature's (IUCN) Red List.
The zoo said, in the wild, they were restricted to "a shrinking pocket of rainforest" around Manaus, Brazil.

summary: Shaldon Wildlife Trust says it is one of two European zoos to breed the species in 2026.

content:
El presidente de Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , dijo que el desplome bursátil de este jueves (05.11.2026) se debió a la contundente victoria de los demócratas en las legislativas de mitad de mandato.
La bolsa cerró en rojo después de la venta masiva de acciones el jueves, impulsada por los temores de que los demócratas pongan en riesgo las inversiones en los centros de datos de la inteligencia artificial.
El índice Nasdaq, que reúne las principales empresas tecnológicas, sufrió su peor retroceso desde abril de 2025.
"El mercado de valores se desplomó hoy porque los 'Dumócratas' tuvieron un gran martes. Es tan triste verlo, ¡solo ustedes tienen la culpa!", publicó Trump en su plataforma Truth Social.
Los centros de datos se han enfrentado a una amplia oposición por parte de los votantes estadounidenses, independientemente de su afiliación política, en gran parte por su impacto ambiental.
Muchos de los ganadores de las elecciones de mitad de legislatura se han comprometido a frenar este tipo de proyectos, que demandan grandes cantidades de agua.
Pérdidas multimillonarias para las 'Siete magníficas'
Las llamadas 'Siete magníficas', las empresas de tecnología más grandes de Estados Unidos, perdieron este jueves conjuntamente más de un billón de dólares.
Las pérdidas las encabezó Tesla (-10,8 %), seguida por Nvidia (-9,3 %), Meta (-4 %), Microsoft (-3,6 %), Alphabet (-2,2 %), Amazon (-2,2 %) y Apple (-1,5 %).
El grupo de 'Big Tech' había subido con fuerza en la víspera, en la jornada posterior a las elecciones de medio mandato, pero en la sesión del jueves borró los 600.000 millones de valor de mercado ganados en esa subida poselectoral, que supuso un hito positivo, y llevó al grupo a anotar el hito negativo de su mayor pérdida conjunta en una sola jornada, de unos 1,13 billones.
Los demócratas arrasan en Estados Unidos
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Las acciones relacionadas con el sector de la IA, sobre todo las vinculadas a la parte de infraestructuras, chips y centros de datos, fueron las grandes perdedoras ante la expectativa de que este sector afronte regulaciones y dificultades para expandir sus centros de datos.
Tesla y SpaceX, las empresas del magnate Elon Musk, gran defensor de la aceleración en el desarrollo de la IA y patrocinador de la victoria electoral del presidente Donald Trump en 2024, borraron en conjunto 420.000 millones de capitalización.
Tras una temporada de campaña marcada por el descontento hacia los centros de datos, las elecciones de mitad de mandato trajeron consigo una oleada de demócratas que prometieron imponer restricciones a estos gigantes que consumen enormes cantidades de energía.
Se espera que, a raíz de esto, surja un entorno normativo más estricto para los gigantes de la inteligencia artificial y los desarrolladores de centros de datos, incluso si el presidente Donald Trump —quizás el mayor defensor de este sector— logra frenar cualquier medida restrictiva a nivel federal.
jc (afp, efe)

media.title: Los demócratas arrasan en Estados Unidos

content:
BBC went to Arizona before the midterms to understand the data centre boom in the US
Published
A US midterms voter poll has suggested data centres were a highly motivating issue for many Americans, leading some to argue public backlash against the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure construction boom might have helped shape the election outcome.
BBC Verify has looked at its role in the campaign and examined the potential consequences for the AI industry.
What did the voter poll suggest?
The poll for AP and a consortium of news organisations found 56% of surveyed voters said data centres were a "crucial or major" factor in their vote, while 76% said they would oppose the construction of a new data centre in their community.
The hostile sentiment was considerably stronger among those who said they voted Democrat at this election.
This follows other recent Pew Research polling, external which suggested about half of Americans think data centres are "mostly bad" for the environment, home energy costs and quality of life, a big deterioration in favourability since January.
The congressional voter poll results certainly suggest a remarkable degree of salience for a subject which likely would not have been on most Americans' radar five years ago.
However, it is some way behind several key issues people considered a "crucial or major factor" in their vote, including government corruption (90%) and the cost of living (89%).
Did the AI backlash affect Senate races?
Three of the Senate seats flipped by the Democrats have significantly more data centres, external, Texas (595), Ohio (258) and Iowa (117), than the median of 55 across all 50 states.
And Texas alone has 31 ongoing data centre construction projects, the most of any state, external.
But other factors would also have been motivating voters in these states, as elsewhere.
BBC Verify analysis of state-level voter polling for Senate elections suggests states which swung to the Democrats either followed the national trend over data centre concerns, or seemed less concerned.
So we can't say how many votes or Senate seats were directly delivered by data centre opposition.
But it's notable that three key states in the US AI build-out, Texas, Georgia and Ohio, all elected Democrats as senators and governors who called for tighter regulation on data centres in one form or another.
These proposals include:
temporary bans on construction
ending tax breaks
requirements to fully cover their own energy and water infrastructure costs
mandates to use unionised construction workers
stricter environmental and transparency safeguards
local rights to veto
What could the election results mean for the future of the AI boom?
The US economy has been heavily supported in recent years by massive corporate investments in AI, external, including for data centre construction.
Official data, external shows inflation-adjusted monthly spending on building data centres, excluding the IT hardware to go into them, in August 2026 was $5bn (£4.2bn) - five times higher than in 2023.
Analysis by Columbia Business School, external suggests AI infrastructure investment in the US is currently larger as a share of the overall economy than spending on new railways was at the height of that boom in the 19th Century.
Cori Crider, executive director of the Future of Tech Institute, a European think tank, told BBC Verify the industry should anticipate that new state leaders will put conditions on or "even stop runaway data centre build".
Seema Shah, from global investment firm Principal Asset Management, said requirements for developers to pay for additional investment in the electricity grid, meet tougher standards over their usage of resources like water, or give up tax incentives could "raise development costs and slow new supply".
The Stargate Oracle AI data centre spans roughly four million square feet in Abilene, Texas
However, Heather West from the Eurasia Group consultancy said temporary bans on construction and new regulations might delay the data centre roll out, but would not stop it entirely.
She said "projects already permitted or under construction will largely proceed", but delays would affect the "next wave" of building through "local fights, slower permitting, and pressure to make data centres pay for their own power".
Analysts from the consultancy Oxford Economics have said there are also strong economic incentives for politicians to avoid policies that would severely disrupt data centre construction, pointing to tax revenue and construction jobs they bring.
Deepak Surana of the Futurum Group, a technology research firm, said he expected there would ultimately be "a negotiation, not a moratorium" from Texas state leaders on data centres to ensure no negative impact on residents' energy and water bills.
OpenAI, which has a data centre in Texas and under-construction projects in Ohio, pledged to ensure it fully paid for its own electricity on Thursday, external - one day after the midterm results.
Additional reporting by Nicholas Barrett, Rob England and Christine Jeavans

BBC Verify logo

summary: BBC Verify examines whether US voters were influenced by the data centre boom - and the impact anti-AI sentiment could have on the industry.

content:
Families of Britons killed in Spain wildfires demand answers
Published
Relatives of Britons killed in this summer's wildfires in Spain have told the BBC they are disgusted, after regional politicians blocked an official inquiry into the disaster.
Nine British nationals were among the 15 people who died when fire ripped through the hillside village of Bédar, in the province of Almería in south-eastern Spain, on 9 July.
Families have criticised the authorities' actions, including the decision not to send an emergency alert to mobile phones as the flames closed in.
"If that evacuation warning had come through in time, my father would still be alive," says Duncan Chard, who blames failures by officials on the day for a number of the deaths.
He lost his father Michael and his dad's partner Christine.
The governing People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox in the Andalusian parliament have rejected a request for a commission of inquiry made by the opposition Socialist party to which Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez belongs.
The PP and Vox argued that an ongoing criminal investigation would provide the necessary answers.
The Andalusian government, PP and Vox have been approached for comment.
Families of those killed say there must be a public and transparent probe.
"It's just outrageous. It's an injustice. As family members, we're absolutely disgusted. This is an insult," says Duncan Chard.
The families also say their grief has been made worse by how police have handled their loved ones' remains and belongings since the fire.
'Issue the damned alert!'
Michael Chard built his house in Bédar from scratch. "He called it Casa Micas," his son said. "It was his place in the sun, it was his little paradise."
On the morning of the fire, Michael's partner Christine had met friends and was due to go to the hairdresser. "Then everything changed... the whole world changed for them," he said.
Christine and Michael Chard are among the 15 people killed in July's deadly wildfire in the village of Bédar
Duncan Chard said his father, who had two artificial knees and walked with a stick, left his house with Christine as soon as they saw the flames. They left their phones and passports behind and tried to escape by car, but the road was blocked.
"This is an action of a brave person who was fighting to the end," he said.
Andalusia's emergencies chief, Antonio Sanz, has said the region decided not to use the system that sends emergency alerts to mobile phones because it could not be tailored to specific communities.
Officials have said some residents needed to evacuate while others were safer staying in their homes. They also argued an alert could have caused panic and traffic jams.
The families reject that.
"Issue the damned alert!" said Chard. "Ring the bells, send the police guy out with his horn, go door to door, do everything."
Thomas-Wolf Verdonckt, a Belgian virologist whose father Stanislas, 63, died, was on the phone to him as the flames approached.
He says the victims "never received advice on what they should do, and certainly not warnings that they were in danger", and that the authorities' claim that everyone in the area was given adequate warning is not true.
"The only contact that the government managed to make with the victims was a couple of minutes before the flames engulfed everyone. One police car drove by with the sirens on. There was no talking, there was no messaging."
Bédar's emergency plan was last approved in 2019, and regional officials say it was in the process of being updated. The municipality is classified by the Andalusian government as being at risk from wildfires.
Of the 15 people who died in Bédar, 14 were foreign nationals: nine British citizens, three Belgian, one French and one American. The other victim was Spanish.
In the days after the fire, Sanz faced a backlash for appearing to blame the victims. He said some people who made the decision to leave "at the last minute, took the wrong path".
Verdonckt has been trying to find answers ever since the blaze.
"The morning afterwards, the Spanish officials brought out... a version of events which was simply the complete opposite of what I experienced," he said.
He also believes a public inquiry is needed to prevent a similar disaster happening in Spain in the future.
"They are putting the safety of citizens in second place. That's simply not okay."
'A huge hole in our lives'
Danni Gillam-Kirton, an assistant headteacher from Nottinghamshire, lost her parents Pete and Fran in the fire.
They had lived in Bédar since 2018. Fran, a former headteacher, ran a quiz night that raised money for the local school and church.
"They were fantastic parents, my biggest champions and cheerleaders," said Danni. "They leave a huge, huge hole in our lives."
She says her mother texted her at about 19:00 to say they had packed in case they had to leave.
"They were waiting for instructions, and those instructions didn't come," she said.
Her parents died on the part of Bédar known as English Hill, one of the places where, families say, the authorities' only contact came minutes before the flames arrived.
Gillam-Kirton says her grief has been made worse by the way the Spanish authorities have behaved since.
Local police had told the family that Pete and Fran's car had been "meticulously searched" by forensic specialists and that she would find nothing.
But in August, a month afterwards, Gillam-Kirton and her husband found what appeared to be human bones in the burnt-out car in which her father died. "I picked up what I recognised to be... part of a pelvis or a hip joint," she said.
Gillam-Kirton fears they were her father's remains.
Within minutes they also found her parents' mobile phones, jewellery, house keys and money. Police had earlier told the family that no personal belongings had survived.
Spain's Guardia Civil police have been approached for comment.
Danni Gillam-Kirton says she found human bones and her parents' possessions in the burnt-out shell of their car
The fragments were eventually sent to Madrid for testing. The family says police have now told them no DNA was recovered and that the bones were those of an animal.
But Gillam-Kirton says experts, including a forensic anthropologist who worked on the Grenfell Tower fire investigation, believe the fragments were human.
"We still don't know who or what they are," she said.
Gillam-Kirton complained to the Guardia Civil. She says the reply told her only that the matter had been passed to the courts, and offered condolences for "the death of your relative", in the singular, when in fact she had lost both her parents.
"It feels like they're going to hope that we exhaust ourselves," she said. "Either the burden of grief is going to be enough for us to give up, or that we're going to financially exhaust ourselves."
Gillam-Kirton says there is "a real lack of empathy when you're dealing with families that have lost so much".
The one thing she wants above all is for someone to acknowledge what went wrong: "No-one seems to be willing to say 'do you know what, we made a mistake and for that we are sorry'."
The death toll in Bédar was the highest from any single fire in Spain during the summer of 2026, and one of the largest in the country's history.
Many victims were trapped as they tried to escape the village, as survivor Malcolm Timbrell told me outside his devastated home in July.
The cause of the disaster, also known as the Los Gallardos fire after the neighbouring town where it started, is the subject of a criminal investigation.
In July, the Guardia Civil said it was believed to have been started by a fallen power line, but that explanation has been called into question.
The BBC has seen a letter in which the Andalusian government refused a request from Socialist MPs for its official reports on the fire. These included any documents explaining why no alert was sent to mobile phones.
Pete (far left) and Fran (far right) both died in the wildfire in July. Danni (second left) wants to know more about what happened to them
The letter, signed by Sanz in September, said the documents could not be released because the criminal investigation is under secreto de sumario, a court order keeping the case file confidential.
Gillam-Kirton says the criminal case is focused on how the fire started, and that it will not necessarily examine the emergency response unless families pay lawyers to put that evidence before the judge.
"How can you have faith in these measures that they're putting in to mitigate future disasters if you don't know fully what happened the first time around?" she said.
"That's why you have a public inquiry," said Duncan Chard, "because the public need answers."
Families in the UK, Belgium and Spain have set up various support groups, as well as a website called helpbedar.com.
They have launched an appeal to pay for legal action, aiming to raise €100,000 (£83,000). Fundraising events are being held in both Spain and the UK, and so far about €11,000 has been collected.
Relatives say their fight is like David and Goliath.
"We are getting steamrolled by the Andalusian government," said Chard.
Ultimately, the families say all they want is answers, and for lessons to be learned so that others do not suffer the same ordeal.
They say they want their fight to be a tribute to their loved ones who died.
"I feel like this is all I can do for them," said Gillam-Kirton.

content:
Asian stocks plunged on November 6, 2026, following a US technology sell-off that erased an estimated US$2.5 trillion from the Nasdaq 100, as investors feared the Democrats’ midterm election victory would slow artificial intelligence (AI) investment.
Japan’s Nikkei entered a bear market and South Korea temporarily halted trading, while Thailand’s SET fell more than 1%. Concerns over possible data centre restrictions compounded doubts about AI investment returns and financing.
Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell more than 20% below its June peak, entering bear-market territory. At 11.50am Bangkok time, the index stood at 57,446.34, down 3,631.56 points, or 5.95%.
Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest lost about 12%, SoftBank Group and memory-chip maker Kioxia about 11% each, and semiconductor equipment supplier Tokyo Electron almost 9%.
South Korea’s Kospi dropped more than 8%, falling below 5,000 and triggering a 20-minute circuit-breaker halt. The smaller-company Kosdaq lost more than 7%.
SK Hynix fell more than 8%, Samsung Electronics 7%, LG Innotek 10% and LG Display 7.7%, reflecting concerns that slower US data centre expansion would weaken AI chip demand.
Taiwan’s Weighted Index lost 2,089.66 points, or 5.03%, to 39,485.06. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world’s largest contract chipmaker, fell 9.6%. Electronics manufacturer Hon Hai Precision Industry, known as Foxconn, lost 9.4%, while Foxconn Technology fell 9.1%.
Elsewhere, Singapore’s Straits Times Index fell 2.4% to 5,169.19; China’s Shenzhen index lost 2.22% and Shanghai Composite 1.14%. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined 1.13%, Malaysia’s benchmark 1.33% and Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 0.82%.
Thailand’s SET lost 16.88 points, or 1.13%, to 1,481.11. All Asian figures were intraday readings.
Before Friday’s falls, the Nikkei and Kospi had gained more than 20% this year, although both had already suffered from Wednesday’s data centre sell-off.
The Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.4% on November 5, its worst session since March 2020. Reuters estimated the market-value loss at US$2.5 trillion, approximately 83.6 trillion baht.
Bloomberg reported that selling began shortly after New York trading opened and intensified throughout the session. All 11 S&P 500 sectors declined, from Nvidia to defensive retailer Walmart.
The three main US indices recorded their worst sessions since President Donald Trump’s April 2025 “Liberation Day” tariff announcement:
- Dow Jones Industrial Average: down 1,833.06 points, or 3.44%, to 51,523.06. - S&P 500: down 334.89 points, or 4.36%, to 7,353.73. - Nasdaq Composite: down 1,421.52 points, or 5.52%, to 24,315.00.
The Nasdaq Composite stood nearly 12% below its October 6 record close, beyond the 10% correction threshold. AI stocks fell for a second consecutive session, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded its fifth decline exceeding 500 points since mid-October.
The Magnificent Seven technology stocks lost more than US$1 trillion collectively. Nvidia shed more than 9%, wiping out over US$440 billion and leaving its shares down 2.6% this year.
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Micron Technology each plunged 17%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which includes Nvidia, Intel and AMD, lost 12%, its worst fall since March 2020, reaching a six-month-plus low and standing more than 38% below its June 22 peak, deep in bear-market territory.
Amazon and Alphabet, which had resisted Wednesday’s AI sell-off, each fell 2.2%.
CoreWeave lost 10% and Nebius 15%, leaving both AI cloud providers down by half or more since October 6. Higher interest rates since late summer and tighter financial conditions had already complicated fundraising.
Five-year credit default swap spreads, reflecting default concerns, reached records of 1,267.9 basis points for CoreWeave and 149.7 for Intel, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Data centre operators Applied Digital, Cipher Digital and IREN each lost more than 14%. Equipment supplier GE Vernova fell 7.4% and power producer Constellation Energy 2.5%.
Microsoft dropped 3.6%. Bloomberg reported that it was tightening oversight of some data centre projects involving Nebius, IREN and Nscale.
Political concerns intensified after the Democrats’ November 3 election victory. Bernie Sanders, Vermont’s independent senator who caucuses with Democrats, called on X for a “National data center moratorium now”, citing local referendums restricting construction.
Sanders argued that Americans opposed technology billionaires damaging the environment, cutting jobs and threatening humanity’s future.
Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, told CNN that data centre work should pause until protections for residents were established.
Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading in Stamford, Connecticut, linked Democratic gains in governorships to a potential construction slowdown.
“The big election outcome was, especially with the Democrats winning a lot of the governorships, that the slowdown of the data center buildout is the real key theme that’s going to stick,” O’Rourke said.
Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management in Plymouth, Massachusetts, anticipated local resistance.
“There’s going to be a lot of pushback about those data centers being geographically located in someone’s backyard, straining the power grid, straining the water systems,” Zaro said.
“Although there are a number of data centers already approved, there are still a lot to be permitted. There’s going to be a difficult road to get those permitted forthcoming,” Zaro added.
UBS analysts estimated that construction pauses could threaten around 30% of expected US data centre capacity additions in 2028, challenging an industry reliant on rapid expansion.
Large earlier share-price gains and questions about returns on enormous AI spending also fuelled concerns. Some analysts questioned whether the sell-off could affect Anthropic’s initial public offering, expected this autumn, with any delay potentially worsening sentiment.
“The market’s moving from the promise of AI to the price of AI,” said Ted Parkhill, founder and chief executive of Incline Investment Management.
“There’s no question that AI is going to be transformative for the world in the long run. But that doesn’t mean every AI-related stock is currently priced appropriately. There’s going to be a lot of turmoil,” Parkhill said.
Investors sought safety in US government bonds. Bloomberg reported that yields across maturities fell by up to 12 basis points to their lowest since early September, while Treasury futures volumes ran about 40% above their 20-day average.
The VIX volatility index jumped 11.57 points to 28.18, its highest since March and its largest increase since December 2024.
October’s US non-farm payrolls report was due on November 6. A Dow Jones poll forecast 59,000 additional jobs, up from September’s 29,000, with unemployment unchanged at 4.2%.
CME FedWatch put the probability of a quarter-percentage-point Federal Reserve rate rise at its December 9 meeting at about 70%.
Victoria Greene, chief investment officer at G Squared Private Wealth, nevertheless viewed the decline as a buying opportunity. Greene favoured memory-chip shares, citing executives’ reports of tight capacity during earnings season.
“The AI trade, in my opinion, is not dead here,” Greene said, describing the sell-off as “a good discount”.

Heavy downpours are expected in Nakhon Si Thammarat and Songkhla on Sunday before expanding to almost all southern provinces along the Gulf of Thailand from Surat Thani.
The Meteorological Department issued a weather alert on Friday for Nakhon Si Thammarat and Songkhla urging the provinces to brace for downpours on Sunday and Monday.
Heavy rain would start in four additional provinces on Monday, it added. They are Surat Thani, Phatthalung, Pattani and Narathiwat.
The department also warned people in the southern provinces of possible flash floods and runoffs triggered by severe storms during the two-day period.
summary: Heavy downpours are expected in Nakhon Si Thammarat and Songkhla on Sunday before expanding to almost all southern provinces along the Gulf of Thailand from Surat Thani.

content:
After the Data Center Policy Committee endorsed the draft policy on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said the Ministry of Finance was preparing to submit the proposed rules to the Cabinet on Tuesday (November 10).
The draft aims to regulate data centres more systematically and balance efforts to attract investment in artificial intelligence (AI) with the need to protect resources and safeguard social interests.
The draft policy covers three main areas.
The Ministry of Digital Economy and Society has been tasked with developing Dashboard TH-DC to bring together information on approvals and permits from all government agencies so they can track projects consistently.
Data centres would be grouped into seven tiers according to their power demand, with requirements tailored to the size of each project.
The proposed standards cover site location and land use, including the storage of oil in reserve for power generation, connections to electricity and water networks, environmental requirements under the Code of Practice (CoP), and economic and social benefits.
Lower-power facilities in tiers 1–4 would be subject to basic requirements and could be located in commercial zones.
Higher-power facilities in tiers 5–7 would face stricter requirements.
The government would give the 63 data centres already operating and the 20 under construction 8–12 months to meet the Code of Practice standards.
Projects that have yet to obtain a licence would be treated as new projects.
More than 100 new projects, with a combined power demand of 3 gigawatts, are waiting to enter the review process.
A subcommittee will assess whether potential sites can meet the projects’ water and electricity needs.
Operators will be able to pitch their plans for review.
The review will consider the benefits for Thailand, including the potential to develop supply chains and give Thai small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) access to computing power.
The first new approvals could come as early as December 2026.

content:
Thai developers are making sports complexes a core feature of property projects to generate recurring income and increase land values, drawing on a sports economy that Savills valued at 238.782 billion baht in 2025.
Savills (Thailand) identifies six or more sports complexes and property projects incorporating sports facilities with disclosed investment, which it puts collectively at more than 10 billion baht. The developments range from private membership clubs for affluent customers and families to public facilities offering court bookings and organised activities.
Sports facilities are increasingly being used to attract visitors to residential and retail developments, encourage longer and more frequent visits, and support spending at restaurants, cafés, shops and health services.
Sansiri is developing S QUARTER in Krungthep Kreetha with investment of approximately 100 million baht. The 3.84-hectare site will offer football, tennis, padel and pickleball facilities, activity studios and cafés, with completion scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2026.
Index Living Mall has invested approximately 80–100 million baht in Talent Sport Academy at The Walk Ratchapruek. Two sports buildings covering about 7,000 square metres accommodate tennis, pickleball and basketball, targeting families and pupils at nearby international schools.
Proud Real Estate plans to redevelop the former Big C site in Bang Yai, covering more than 4.32 hectares, into a mixed-use project with an arena, sports club and sports complex serving sports tourism and wellness customers.
K.E. Group’s Crystal Sports project beside the Ram Inthra expressway is planned as a premium tennis community with nine indoor courts.
Eden Country Club is among the major membership developments, with approximately 2.4 billion baht earmarked for a 3.84-hectare site on Bang Na–Trat Road. Tennis and padel courts, a racket sports centre, swimming pools and wellness facilities are planned, with full operations targeted for 2028.
Reignwood Sports and Performance Center represents investment of about 1.4 billion baht within Reignwood Park. The wider development combines the exclusive Robinswood Golf Club, housing and an international school.
Among facilities accessible to the public, The O2 Bangkok in Bang O, near an MRT station, is a four-storey sports building covering approximately 10,200 square metres. Its investment is about 200 million baht, with badminton, basketball, five-a-side football, fitness and rehabilitation facilities.
Sterling Sport & Wellness on Sukhumvit soi 24 combines tennis, padel and pickleball with exercise studios and physiotherapy. THEA Sports Club is planned for the Phran Nok–Kanchanaphisek area in western Bangkok.
Figures presented by Savills show participation in physical activity rising from 87.26% in 2024 to 89.7% in 2025 and 91.7% in the first half of 2026, an increase of 4.44 percentage points over that period. The share not exercising fell to 8.3%.
Reported average sports spending per person was highest among people aged 30–39, at approximately 7,700 baht, followed by those aged 40–49 at 7,600 baht and those aged 60–69 at 7,300 baht.
Working adults, families and older people bring different requirements, from health and recreational sport to rehabilitation and wellness, giving operators scope to serve several customer groups.
Demand extends beyond gyms and organised sport to walking, running, cycling and outdoor recreation. The range of activities creates demand for fitness centres, sports grounds, pools, running tracks, green spaces and outdoor activity areas within residential developments.
Thailand’s sports economy accounted for 1.26% of gross domestic product in 2025, its highest recorded share, according to figures presented by Savills.
Data from the National Sports Development Fund and the Tourism and Sports Ministry put direct economic value at approximately 176 billion baht and indirect value at about 62 billion baht.
Sports-related economic activity extends beyond competitions to sporting goods, fitness facilities, sports grounds, food and beverages, hotels, tourism and travel to sporting activities, creating opportunities across consumption and services.
A 2026 assessment by the World Economic Forum and Oliver Wyman puts the global sports economy at approximately US$2.3 trillion annually, with a projection of US$3.7 trillion by 2030.
Most projects identified by Savills cluster around suburban Bangkok, particularly Bang Na–Trat and Krungthep Kreetha in the east, Ratchapruek and Phran Nok–Kanchanaphisek in the west, and Bang O on the Thon Buri side.
Suburban locations offer larger plots and development costs below those in the central business district, while remaining close to family housing and international schools. Sports complexes require substantial space for courts and multiple activities, making land availability more restrictive than for conventional commercial projects.
Larger developments are taking the form of sports cities combining sport, health, education, housing and services. Woraluk Property’s AREA 340 in Bang Sai district, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, covers approximately 192 hectares, with planned investment exceeding 5 billion baht.
AREA 340 will include sports grounds, golf, housing, educational and health facilities, and community spaces. Cooperation with Kasetsart University covers the development of sports science and sports management courses, with project completion planned for 2029.
Savills’ disclosed investment tally comprises AREA 340, Eden Country Club, Reignwood Sports and Performance Center, The O2 Bangkok, S QUARTER and Talent Sport Academy. Investment values have not been disclosed for THEA Sports Club, Crystal Sports and Arena Bangkok Club.
Savills expects further investment in 2027, particularly in suburban locations and economically important cities capable of accommodating larger developments.
For landowners, sports facilities can improve land use, attract residents, visitors and related businesses, and increase surrounding property values. Membership fees, court hire and health services can provide recurring revenue.
Savills cautions that success depends on location, local purchasing power, the customer catchment, the selection of sports and facilities, and operating partners’ capabilities. Projects require both substantial initial investment and sustained operations, making the business model as important as demand for sport.
Source: Thansettakij

content:
Beau Lamarre-Condon “stands by” his decision to shoot Jesse Baird but did not intend to kill him, the New South Wales supreme court has heard.
The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
Lamarre-Condon continued giving evidence in the double murder trial on Friday, telling the court about the moment he allegedly shot Baird.
“That first shot into Jesse’s right shoulder was the right move. I stand by it,” he said.
He claimed Baird had lunged at him with a knife and told the court he deliberately aimed his gun at the right shoulder, believing it would not kill Baird.
“As police officers we are trained to shoot people at the centre of body mass … I had a split-second moment where I said, ‘Drop the knife’ … It was just police mode now,” he said from the witness box.
“If I didn’t do that I was 110% going to have that knife driven into my throat.”
However, Lamarre-Condon repeatedly told the court he “did not want to kill Jesse”.
“Jesse did not deserve anything like that to happen to him,” he told the court.
“He did nothing to me to deserve to be killed.”
During his second day in the witness box, Lamarre-Condon told the jury he entered Baird’s home on 19 February 2024 because he wanted to retrieve his belongings from the house without being recognised.
He claimed he did not want to come into contact with Baird due to a risk the other man could take out an apprehended violence order against him as Baird had previously asked him to “please refrain from contacting me”.
Lamarre-Condon told the court he had seen what he assumed to be someone’s delivery motorcycle: “As soon as I saw that I had an idea … I saw a hi-vis hooded jacket, waterproof long pants and gloves.
“This moment here … I wish that I didn’t do this … But I had the thought process that if I was to put on this helmet and outfit I could knock on Jesse’s door I would look like an UberEats driver without any verbal interaction with Jesse.”
The accused thought Baird’s room was empty when he entered the home, he told the court.
He looked through some storage boxes in Baird’s home in search of his belongings, including a Cartier ring and a $2,000 shirt, but could not find them, he said.
When he looked up, he saw Baird with a knife and tape, sealing boxes, and said the other man began yelling, “We’re getting robbed,” the jury heard.
Lamarre-Condon said he was still wearing the motorcycle helmet and had his firearm in a holster under his shirt when Baird saw him.
“He started yelling, ‘We’re getting robbed, we’re getting robbed,’ … He couldn’t see it was me because the visor was down,” Lamarre-Condon said.
He told the court Baird pinned him against a wall with his left forearm while “swinging around the knife” in his other hand as the officer yelled: “It’s Beau, calm the fuck down.”
He said he then had a “very, very clear thought”.
“[I thought] shoot him in the shoulder so you don’t kill him, so he drops the knife,” he told the court.
Lamarre-Condon claimed he then fired the gun, but the two continued to struggle and the officer’s finger remained on the trigger, the jury heard.
after newsletter promotion
They tripped over a storage box on the ground, which is when Lamarre-Condon “accidentally” discharged the gun.
He told the court: “It was my fault … I am guilty of manslaughter … But it wasn’t intentional.”
Under cross-examination from crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC, Lamarre-Condon repeated that he “stands by” the decision to take the first shot.
“If I didn’t, Mr Crown, you would be sitting here today interrogating Mr Baird,” he said.
Asked by Hatfield if he shot Baird in the back, Lamarre-Condon said: “That’s not accurate, that’s not true.”
While Lamarre-Condon said Baird’s shooting was his fault, he maintained Davies shot himself.
After the first two shots, the jury heard that Lamarre-Condon dialled the emergency hotline to try to get help for Baird.
But when he looked up, he saw Davies, who he didn’t recognise at the time.
The accused claimed the other man had picked up his gun.
“It was pointed towards me at my chest and he said: ‘I’m going to fucking shoot you,’” he told the court.
“I started lowering my body towards the ground. I said, ‘Please don’t shoot me, I’m not here to shoot you. I’m not a threat I’m not here to hurt you.’
“That’s when he raised the gun towards my head and said, ‘Fuck off.’”
The former officer said police are trained to redirect gun muzzles when firearms are pointed at them.
“I saw the gun, he was holding it with both hands, I thought, ‘fuck he’s going to fire the gun’ and that’s where my police training kicked in,” he told the court.
“My left hand would have grabbed Luke’s left wrist and turned it away … my other hand pushed against the forearm and then I pushed the pivot point of the left wrist away from me.”
Asked by the defence lawyer whether the gun went off, Lamarre-Condon said: “Yes, during this motion. And it got Luke.”
Baird’s mother, Helen, left the courtroom partway through Lamarre-Condon’s evidence.
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

FRANKFURT — After decades of making bumper profits in China, Germany's carmakers have run out of road and sales have slumped dramatically, forcing painful job losses at home.
Volkswagen's woes in China pushed Europe's largest carmaker to a €5.8-billion (US$6.5--billion) loss for the three months to end-September.
The 10-brand group's declining fortunes in the world's largest car market are the main reason behind a historic restructuring drive that could see it shed up to 120,000 jobs by the end of the decade.
BMW (Bayerische Motoren Werke) and Mercedes-Benz are also cutting jobs, and all three have issued profit warnings this year.
"Nobody was prepared for the swiftness or the violence of the pivot," Tu Le of Sino Auto Insights told Agence France-Presse (AFP). "The fall for the German automakers has been really abrupt."
The big three German carmakers' annual vehicle deliveries in China fell about a third between 2019 and 2025 to 3.87 million, according to AFP calculations based on company disclosures.
Chinese carmakers' shares of their domestic market meanwhile rose to 65.3 from 37.8%, according to the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA).
'Disbelief'
The rapid fall has come as a shock to Germany, a nation that has regarded itself as a key player ever since Carl Benz invented the motor car in 1886.
German carmakers' rich history meant they were long dismissive of Chinese competition and slow to react, said a former Mercedes-Benz strategy expert who later consulted for BMW.
"When I was doing analyses of the market in China there was not appreciation, more a sort of confusion," she told AFP.
"It was coming from a place of elitism, a thought of 'Oh we're better'. There was disbelief that others could do things differently."
The German brands meanwhile had to compete with the likes of China's BYD (Build Your Dreams), which started out making batteries for mobile phones, and Xpeng, founded by software entrepreneur He Xiaopeng.
The Chinese government stepped up support for electric vehicles (EVs) with subsidies and charging infrastructure at the same time.
That made Germans' key strength -- long experience in improving internal combustion engines -- increasingly irrelevant and perhaps soon obsolete.
"What the market demanded was not a skillset they had", Le said. "The legacy automakers in China were bringing analogue toys to a digital party."
Looking east
Germany's carmakers have held up better in China's combustion-engine segment. Volkswagen is the country's number-one carmaker for petrol and diesel vehicles.
But that is a wasting asset in China, where so-called new energy vehicles made up a record 67.8 percent of sales last month, according to the CPCA, leaving combustion-engine cars looking tired.
"In China people associate brands with specific technologies now. If you think of Volkswagen, you think petrol, not electric," Ingo Speich of Deka Investment, which holds shares in the German carmakers, told AFP.
"It's like after 2007 when Apple invented the iPhone. Nokia started coming out with good smartphones by 2009, 2010, but it was too late, people just didn't think of them as smartphone-makers."
Germany's carmakers are now trying to shift engineering east, both to stay competitive in the Chinese market as well as to integrate technologies developed there into cars sold abroad.
Volkswagen said a year ago that it could now design cars from start to finish in China at its centre in Hefei.
Both BMW and VW have said they hope to export vehicles from China into other parts of the Asia-Pacific region.
The low-cost Volkswagen ID.Every1, slated for European launch in 2027, will meanwhile have an electric motor made in China.
"You can see us also as a Chinese player", Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume said in July. "We can do the same as the Chinese can do."
Speaking in October, Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Kaellenius said the company would overhaul its China strategy, adding that giving up on the world's toughest but largest market was not an option.
"We're not looking at China as something (like), 'Oh that's going away and let's focus on the other things'," he said.
"There's not a play where you put China aside."

Thailand’s Treasury Department will begin selling and exchanging three types of commemorative coins on November 6, 2026, to mark the fourth-cycle, or 48th, birthday anniversary of Her Majesty Queen Suthida Bajrasudhabimalalakshana on June 3, 2026.
The collection, produced by the Ministry of Finance through the Treasury Department, comprises gold, silver and copper-nickel coins. Prices range from 20 baht for the standard commemorative coin to 99,999 baht for the limited-edition gold version.
Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas explained that the coins were created to honour the Queen’s dedication to royal duties and her contributions to public welfare.
He noted that Her Majesty had undertaken numerous royal responsibilities with diligence and ability, helping improve people’s well-being while demonstrating exemplary conduct.
The commemorative issue is also intended to promote recognition of the Queen’s royal contributions in Thailand and abroad, while giving members of the public an opportunity to collect the coins as a tribute to Her Majesty.
The Treasury Department has produced three versions, each with different specifications, prices and maximum mintages.
1. Proof gold commemorative coin
The gold coin has a face value of 50,000 baht and contains 99% gold. It measures 26 millimetres in diameter and weighs 15 grammes.
Each coin will be sold for 99,999 baht, with production limited to 1,000 pieces.
2. Proof silver commemorative coin
The silver version has a face value of 1,000 baht and contains 92.5% silver. It has a diameter of 35 millimetres and weighs 22 grammes.
The selling price is 3,000 baht per coin, with a maximum production of 5,000 pieces.
3. Copper-nickel commemorative coin
The standard-finish coin has a face value of 20 baht and is made from an alloy containing 75% copper and 25% nickel.
Measuring 32 millimetres in diameter and weighing 15 grammes, it can be exchanged at its face value of 20 baht.
Production will be limited to 250,000 pieces.
The front of each coin features a portrait of Her Majesty Queen Suthida wearing earrings and traditional Thai royal attire.
Her Majesty is depicted wearing the sash of the Most Illustrious Order of the Royal House of Chakri, together with a diamond-encrusted brooch and several royal decorations.
These include the insignia of the First Class of the Order of Chula Chom Klao, the First Class Royal Cypher Medals of Kings Rama IX and Rama X, and the Gold Ratcharuchi Medal of King Rama X.
The portrait also features commemorative medals marking the 2019 Royal Coronation and King Rama X’s sixth-cycle, or 72nd, birthday anniversary in 2024.
Her Majesty’s full royal name is inscribed along the lower edge of the coin.
The reverse features portraits of Their Majesties the King and Queen undertaking royal duties associated with four development initiatives.
These are the Bueng Si Fai commemorative development project, Prem Prachawanarak Park, the Bo Din Khao Pond Development Project and a large-scale groundwater supply project designed to address drought.
An inscription around the upper edge commemorates the Queen’s fourth-cycle birthday anniversary on June 3, 2026, and identifies Thailand as the issuing country. The denomination of each coin appears along the lower edge.
Treasury Department Director-General Theeralak Saengsanit confirmed that members of the public can purchase or exchange the commemorative coins from November 6 onwards.
In Bangkok and surrounding areas, the coins will be available through the Treasury Department’s Currency Management Division and designated coin receiving and exchange units.
Provincial residents can obtain the coins through Treasury offices in all 76 provinces.
The coins will also be available through the Treasury Department’s online service.
The three versions are priced at 99,999 baht for the proof gold coin, 3,000 baht for the proof silver coin and 20 baht for the copper-nickel coin.

content:
Thailand’s annual headline inflation reached 3.90% in October 2026, driven by a 29.18% increase in fuel prices, while the Commerce Ministry maintained its full-year inflation forecast at 2.0%.
Nantapong Chiralerspong, director-general of the Trade Policy and Strategy Office (TPSO), reported that core inflation, which excludes fresh food and energy, stood at 1.58%. Average headline inflation for January–October was 1.77% compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.
Higher fuel prices reflected continuing pressure from the Middle East energy crisis following attacks on Saudi Arabian oil-producing areas. Average Dubai crude prices reached their highest level in seven months.
Prices in the vehicles, transport and communications category rose 10.93% year on year. Increases covered fuel, school transport, interprovincial van services, air-conditioned buses, motorcycle taxis, minibuses and songthaews (shared pick-up taxis).
The broader non-food and beverage category recorded a 3.66% increase. Recreation, reading, education and religious activities rose 1.51%, with higher costs for domestic and overseas tours, travel to visit relatives and make merit, and pet food.
The tobacco and alcoholic beverages category increased 0.04%, with beer and wine among the items becoming more expensive.
Food and non-alcoholic beverage prices increased 4.26% year on year. Flooding in important vegetable-growing areas pushed up some fresh vegetable prices early in October, although prices gradually returned towards normal levels towards the end of the month.
Prepared food prices rose 4.06%, including ready-made dishes, noodles, rice with curry, rice served with holy basil stir-fries, and fried rice.
Fresh vegetables becoming more expensive included limes, holy basil, Chinese kale, aubergines, spring onions, yardlong beans and Chinese flowering cabbage.
Prices also increased for pork, fresh chicken, fresh and steamed mackerel, whiteleg shrimp and squid. Within the rice, flour and flour products group, white rice, glutinous rice and sandwich bread became more expensive.
Non-alcoholic beverage prices rose 1.94%, including purified drinking water, soft drinks, instant coffee, and hot and iced coffee. Other increases covered sweets, ice cream, brown sugar, fish sauce, shrimp paste, vegetable oil, monosodium glutamate, seasonings and soy sauce.
The eggs and dairy products category increased 6.90%, with higher prices for chicken and duck eggs, soya milk and fermented milk drinks.
Fresh fruit prices fell 0.15%, with declines recorded for longkong, mangoes, dragon fruit and Nam Wa bananas.
Electricity prices declined, alongside charges for contracted home repairs covering labour and materials. Household items becoming cheaper included bedsheets, blankets, bathroom and floor cleaners, towels, washing machines and air conditioners.
Personal care products also recorded price declines, including skin protection and skincare products, hair conditioner, perfume, soap, face powder, facial cleansers and toothpaste.
Clothing and footwear becoming cheaper included men’s and women’s shirts and trousers, men’s trainers and children’s T-shirts.
The Commerce Ministry retained its forecast for average headline inflation in 2026 at 1.8–2.2%, with a midpoint of 2.0%.
Nantapong expects inflation to remain positive in November. Factors to monitor include elevated global energy prices, prepared food and transport costs, and weather conditions affecting some agricultural products.
Government energy measures, the Commerce Ministry’s price monitoring and easing floods are expected to help reduce price pressures and household living costs.
The latest international comparison, based on September figures, placed Thailand’s headline inflation of 2.82% as the 37th-lowest among 139 reporting economies.
Thailand also recorded the fifth-lowest rate among the 10 ASEAN economies included in the comparison, below Indonesia, Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines and Laos.

Panadda "Boom" Wongphudee has sought to apologise to the public after being arrested at her house on Friday as her husband, Atip "Got" Anantawan, surrendered to authorities to fight serious charges, including public fraud and money laundering.
Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) authorities arrested the 50-year-old actress outside her residence at 6.30am in Bueng Kum district of Bangkok.
The arrest followed warrants issued for the couple on Thursday evening, and police waited until daybreak the following day to take action. Ms Panadda, who is a social activist and president of the Goodness Foundation, had been waiting in her house with her lawyer since she learned about the warrants.
CIB officers also searched her residence after the arrest and another team went inside her two foundation offices in Thanya Buri district of Pathum Thani and Bang Khen district in Bangkok, looking for more evidence to substantiate the charges.
Pol Maj Gen Thatphum Jaruprat, the Economic Crime Suppression Division commander, said officers have now searched four locations in Bangkok and vicinity and were collecting all the evidence seized to sort and classify.
Atip Anantawan, Panadda Wongphudee's husband, right, arrives at the Crime Suppression Division to surrender to authorities, a day after arrest warrants were issued for the couple. (Photo supplied/Wassayos Ngamkham)
Mr Atip, who is a real estate investor and fitness professional, arrived at the Crime Suppression Division, a unit under the CIB, to surrender to authorities, a day after the arrest warrants were issued.
While being escorted to the CIB by investigators, Ms Panadda apologised to the public and said she was ready to face the judicial process.
Wearing a black suit and appearing exhausted, Ms Panadda gave a wai, a traditional Thai gesture of apology and told reporters briefly: “I am ready to enter the judicial process, and I would like to apologise to everyone.”
Meanwhile, police have frozen 18 bank accounts containing about 102 million baht belonging to people linked to Ms Panadda and her foundation.
Another 30 accounts have also been frozen. These accounts had received transfers from Ms Panadda's personal accounts and those of the Goodness Foundation, and contained a further 2 million baht.
Other assets have yet to be frozen as investigators were still examining the full extent of the assets involved.
Pol Maj Gen Thatphum said Ms Panadda faces three charges: colluding to defraud the public, conspiring to commit money laundering, and entering false information into a computer system.
Her husband has been charged with a single offence — conspiring to commit money laundering.
Police expected to bring the suspects to the Criminal Court to seek approval to detain them no later than Saturday.

The Group’s improved performance was primarily driven by growth in the energy business, both gas-fired and renewable energy businesses. For the gas-fired power business, Gulf Pluak Daeng (GPD), an IPP project under the IPD group, recorded higher core profit compared to the same period last year, supported by increased electricity sales to the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT). The average load factor rose from 45% in Q3/2025 to 72% in Q3/2026. The Company also recognized a share of core profit of THB 350 million from the Hin Kong Power (HKP) project, an increase of 61% from THB 218 million in Q3/2025, when unit 1 underwent a scheduled A-inspection. In addition, the Company recognized a share of core profit of THB 562 million from the GJP group in Q3/2026, an increase of 2% from THB 550 million in Q3/2025. This was mainly driven by higher electricity sales to EGAT from the GJP group’s two IPP projects, Gulf Uthai (GUT) and Gulf Nong Saeng (GNS). In Q3/2026, the average load factors of GUT and GNS increased to 18% and 37%, respectively.
This improvement partly offset a slight decline in profit from the GJP group’s seven SPP projects due to higher natural gas costs and a lower Ft rate. The Company also recognized a share of core profit of THB 932 million from the Jackson Generation gas-fired power project in the United States, an increase of 67% from THB 557 million in Q3/2025. This was mainly driven by a significant rise in the Capacity Payment, reflecting higher electricity demand from data centers in the PJM market. The average Capacity Payment increased from USD 270 per MW per day in Q3/2025 to USD 329 per MW per day in Q3/2026. The project also benefited from a wider spark spread as power prices rose in response to increased demand, particularly during the heatwave in July 2026.
For the renewable energy business, in Q3/2026, the Company recognized higher core profit from domestic solar farm and solar farm with battery energy storage system (solar BESS) projects following the commercial operation of additional projects. The Company currently has 14 domestic solar farm and solar BESS projects in operation, with a combined installed capacity of 1,379 MW, compared with five projects with a combined installed capacity of 532 MW in Q3/2025. The Company also recognized a share of core profit of THB 319 million from wind power projects under the Gulf Gunkul group in Q3/2026, an increase of 38% from THB 230 million in Q3/2025. The improvement was driven by higher average wind speeds, which rose from 5.7 m/s in Q3/2025 to 6.5 m/s in Q3/2026. Meanwhile, the Mekong Wind (MKW) project in Vietnam also performed better, following the finalization of a new power tariff with Vietnam Electricity (EVN). The electricity tariff increased from 3.9 US cents per kWh in Q3/2025 to 7.2 US cents per kWh in Q3/2026, while curtailment declined from 5% to 1%.
The resources business recorded an overall improvement in Q3/2026, mainly due to the LNG import business under GLNG and HKH, which benefited from higher import volumes and the implementation of the LNG optimization strategy. During the first nine months of 2026, the Company imported 56 LNG cargoes, equivalent to approximately 3.7 million tons. However, the share of core profit from the PTT NGD project declined by 7%, from THB 199 million in Q3/2025 to THB 184 million in Q3/2026, due to losses from derivative instruments, despite an increase in gross profit.
The digital business under the Gulf Edge group returned to profit in Q3/2026, compared with a loss in the same period last year. This followed the GSA01 data center’s commencement of full operations in June 2026, with customers gradually occupying the entire leased space.
In Q3/2026, the Company recognized a share of core profit from AIS of THB 4,443 million, representing an increase of 16% from THB 3,829 million in Q3/2025. The growth was mainly driven by AIS’s improved operating performance, supported by higher average revenue per user (ARPU) in both mobile and fixed broadband businesses, growth in handset sales, and lower network and spectrum costs. Total dividend income from the Company’s investments amounted to THB 474 million in Q3/2026, up from THB 276 million in Q3/2025. The increase was mainly attributable to higher dividends from KBANK following an increase in the Company’s investment stake.
In Q3/2026, the Company reported earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of THB 15,265 million, an increase of 12% from THB 13,641 million in Q3/2025. Net profit attributable to the parent company, including foreign exchange impacts, was THB 9,289 million, up 28% from THB 7,274 million in Q3/2025.
As of 30 September 2026, the Company reported total assets of THB 841,610 million, total liabilities of THB 478,774 million, and shareholders’ equity of THB 362,836 million. The net interest-bearing debt to equity ratio was 1.02 times, down from 1.06 times as of 30 June 2026, reflecting an increase in shareholders’ equity following the Group’s improved operating performance.
Mr. Smith Banomyong, Chief Financial Officer, stated, “The Company continues to project total revenue and EBITDA growth of approximately 12–15% in 2026. In Q4/2026, we expect continued growth in operating performance, particularly from the renewable energy business. Four domestic solar farm and solar BESS projects, with a combined installed capacity of 373 MW, are scheduled to commence commercial operation from late November through December 2026. In addition, solar rooftop projects under GULF1 are expected to supply approximately 30 MW of additional electricity to customers in Q4/2026. The fourth quarter is also the high season for wind power generation, and the three wind projects under the Gulf Gunkul group in Thailand and the BKR2 project in Germany are expected to deliver improved performance.
In 2027, the Company expects several new power projects with a combined installed capacity of more than 600 MW to commence commercial operation. These comprise two domestic solar power projects with a combined capacity of 133 MW, five domestic wind power projects with a combined capacity of 376 MW, 12 industrial waste-to-energy projects with a combined capacity of 118 MW, and three solid recovered fuel (SRF) facilities.
In the infrastructure business, the Bang Pa-in–Nakhon Ratchasima Intercity Motorway (M6) is scheduled to commence commercial operations in Q2/2027. In the data center business, GSA02, located in Chonburi in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC), has a maximum service capacity of 38.1 MW and is scheduled to commence operations in Q2/2027. GEDC01, located in Rayong in the EEC, has a maximum service capacity of 100 MW and is scheduled to commence operations in Q4/2027.
Over the longer term, GULF sees opportunities to expand its business under the draft Power Development Plan (PDP 2026), which is expected to open opportunities to develop gas-fired and renewable power projects. The Direct PPA program, which will allow electricity trading from a broader range of energy sources and not only renewables, together with community solar farm projects, will create further opportunities for the Company to develop projects and expand its business while supporting rising demand for clean energy. Beyond energy, the Company is continuing to build its digital business, which has growth potential alongside the digital transformation, particularly in data centers, cloud, and AI. The Company plans to expand its data center business while developing digital infrastructure and related businesses to support growing demand for digital and AI services, pursue further business opportunities, and support GULF’s long-term growth.”

Thailand's Royal Barge Procession will be broadcast live on Friday (November 6, 2026), as Their Majesties the King and Queen travel along the Chao Phraya River to Wat Arun Ratchawararam in Bangkok for the Royal Kathin robe-offering ceremony.
The live broadcast, organised by the Television Pool of Thailand, will begin at 2.30pm, while the royal journey is scheduled to start from Wasukri Pier at 3pm.
The ceremony forms part of celebrations marking Her Majesty Queen Suthida's fourth-cycle, or 48th, birthday anniversary, which fell on June 3, 2026.
Members of the public are invited to watch the procession along the Chao Phraya River and welcome Their Majesties at designated viewing areas.
The Government Public Relations Department (PRD) will provide live coverage through television, radio and online platforms.
Television
Radio
YouTube
The live coverage will allow viewers across Thailand to follow the procession and the royal ceremony at Wat Arun.
Authorities have designated 16 locations along both banks of the Chao Phraya River where members of the public can watch the Royal Barge Procession and welcome Their Majesties.
The locations are:
The viewing locations provide opportunities for residents and visitors to witness the procession from both sides of the river as Their Majesties travel towards Wat Arun.
Members of the public planning to attend can check the procession route and transport arrangements before travelling.
The Royal Thai Navy has published information about the procession, including its route and preparations.
The Royal Barge Procession and Royal Kathin ceremony will take place on November 6, with live television, radio and online coverage beginning at 2.30pm.
